claims.text: The initial material is an as-cast HfZrTiTa0.53 refractory multicomponent alloy.
The baseline alloy has a yield strength of approximately 786 MPa.
The baseline alloy has a compressive strength of approximately 1314 MPa.
The baseline alloy has approximately 13.5% terminal tensile strain.
The alloy should be cold rolled to a 50–70% reduction.
Cold rolling should be followed by controlled annealing at 600–700 °C.
The proposed annealing treatment will enable recovery and grain refinement without full recrystallization.
Cold rolling introduces high dislocation density and deformation heterogeneities.
The treatment will produce an ultrafine-grained microstructure with a more uniform grain-size distribution and fewer stress concentrators.
The refined microstructure will promote grain-boundary sliding and more uniform activation of slip systems.
Reduced local stress concentrations will delay tensile necking.
The treatment will increase uniform tensile elongation by at least approximately 50%, from a stated baseline of about 13.5% to over 20%.
The treatment will preserve a yield strength of approximately 786 MPa.
The treatment will preserve a compressive strength of approximately 1314 MPa.
The treatment will preserve comparable impact-triggered chemical energy release.
The tensile prediction applies at room temperature and quasi-static strain rates below 10^-3 s^-1.
Excessive grain growth or recrystallization could reduce strength and impact properties.
The predicted trend may not hold at extremely high strain rates or substantially different temperatures.

contradictions.description: The 13.5% value is variously treated as terminal strain, terminal tensile strain, and the baseline for uniform tensile elongation. Terminal strain and uniform elongation are distinct metrics, so the claimed 50% improvement lacks a consistently defined baseline.

The prediction concerns uniform tensile elongation, but the measurement list defines it parenthetically as strain to failure. Uniform elongation ends at necking and is not generally equivalent to total strain to failure.
